pure-announcement.rationale: Google's own launch post for A2A: a launch-partner roll call, vision framing, and roughly two-thirds of the text is partner endorsement quotes; the protocol mechanics are a promotional summary of the linked draft spec, which is the actual primary source.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept covers an agent-to-agent interoperability protocol; the corpus neighbours are skills, governance and observability concepts.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The draft specification and code samples are linked and independently checkable.

durability.rationale: Anchored to launch-day state — a draft spec, 'production-ready later this year', and a 50-partner roster — which is exactly the adoption-list content that ages badly even though the protocol itself lived on.

actionability.rationale: Five design principles and a candidate-sourcing vignette describe the landscape; a builder gets nothing to act on beyond links to the spec.

atomicity.rationale: A single idea — an open client/remote agent protocol with capability discovery via Agent Cards, a task lifecycle producing artifacts, and modality-negotiated message parts — statable in one paragraph.
